headline: Growth accelerates across both segments, tops guidance
summary_short: Arrow Electronics' Q2 2026 revenue rose 31.8% y/y to $9,992M, above the high end of its own guidance, with operating income up 98.0% y/y to $377M and diluted EPS up 46.5% y/y to $5.26, while long-term debt fell 13.2% y/y to $2,053M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 31.8% y/y (30% constant currency) to $9,992M, led by Global Components +39% y/y to $7,366M and Global ECS +14% y/y to $2,627M; FX added $93.5M to sales. Operating income rose 98% y/y to $377M as Components operating income more than doubled, partly offset by a 12% y/y decline in ECS operating income tied to losses on certain non-cancellable purchase obligations. Net income rose 45% y/y to $273M ($5.26 diluted EPS, $5.45 non-GAAP), both above the high end of prior guidance. Arrow guided Q3 2026 sales to $9.60B-$10.20B and diluted EPS to $4.72-$4.92. Cash fell to $245M after $300M of net debt repayment and $43M of buybacks; long-term debt fell 13.2% y/y to $2,053M.

drivers.explanation: Sales rose 32% y/y (30% constant currency), driven by Global Components +39% y/y and Global ECS +14% y/y; currency effects added $93.5 million to revenue and $0.09 to diluted EPS versus the prior-year quarter.

Not explicitly explained at the consolidated level; Global Components segment margin rose to 11.6% from 11.2% y/y while Global ECS margin fell to 10.2% from 11.2% y/y, so the blended increase reflects mix shift toward faster-growing Components.

Global Components operating income rose 112% y/y to $396 million on sales growth and margin gains, while Global ECS operating income fell 12% y/y to $85 million on losses tied to underperformance of certain non-cancellable multi-year purchase obligations.

Not separately explained in the release; follows from operating income growth of 98% y/y, which outpaced a much smaller gain on investments ($12.0M vs $104.0M a year ago) and lower interest expense ($37.3M vs $60.3M).
Not separately explained in the release; follows from net income growth of 45% y/y combined with a slightly lower diluted share count (51.9M vs 52.3M y/y) from ongoing buybacks.

Arrow generated $318 million of operating cash flow ('partly due to the timing of cash flows within Global Components supply chain services offerings'), but $300 million of net debt repayment and $42 million of buybacks left quarter-end cash at $245 million, down from $287 million.
Long-term debt fell as Arrow made $300 million of net repayments on long-term bank borrowings during the quarter, per the cash-flow statement.

Management cites broad-based demand across regions and end markets in both Global Components and Global ECS, book-to-bill ratios 'well above parity,' and a growing backlog, framing results as evidence of durable, higher-margin, value-added growth and disciplined capital allocation.
